title: Weight-Space Programming Changes How an LLM Uses Python for Computational Biology
read_level: full (v1 PDF; supplementary Table S1 not in PDF text)
why_wsp: Claude Opus 5.5 (Editor) inspects Qwen3.5-0.8B's tensors and responses and directly edits its weights via WSP harness tools, without gradient training, to improve tool-using computational biology problem solving.
domain: computational biology problems with Python tool use (melting temperature, entropy, enzyme kinetics, codon optimization)
editor: Claude Opus 5.5 (via API); analysis of traces by Codex (GPT-6.1 Sol)
target: Qwen3.5-0.8B, BF16, thinking enabled, served with vLLM
interface: code/tensor tools (inspect tensors, CPU calculations, WSP harness weight-modification tools, evaluate on editing problems)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (target-call budget up to 10 successful evaluation calls per editing run)
self_editing: no; Claude edits a separate Qwen model
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: Per checkpoint: "64,409" (seed 1), "51,892,555" (seed 2, 24 matrices in blocks 12-23), "616,799" (seed 3), "1,019" (seed 4) changed scalar weights; seeds 1, 3, 4 confined to 'MLP down-projection' of block 23 (Table 2)

headline_results.quote: the number of responses graded as strictly correct increased from 44 (7.3%) for the original model to 77 (12.8%) for the edited models
the number of correct responses increased from 64 (10.7%) to 100 (16.7%), with an increase in each of the four editing runs
Total Python calls fell from 5,599 to 3,479 after editing, and calls repeating an earlier syntax tree fell from 1,834 to 1,044

headline_results.claim: Most edited-only gains were already computed by original
headline_results.quote: Of the 64 pairs in which only the edited response was technically correct, 13 showed a correction to the target computation in the executed Python code. In 36 pairs, the original model had already computed the correct value
Across the six additional checkpoints, technically correct responses increased from 96 to 154 in 900 pairs
Completed responses that failed the technical correctness criterion also increased, from 42 to 274.

headline_results.claim: T17: fewer correct Python outputs, more correct answers
headline_results.quote: correct Python outputs decreased from 60 to 22 after editing, while strictly correct final answers increased from 0 to 15 and technically correct final answers from 0 to 18
After editing, this count increased for 17 of the 50 problems, stayed the same for 27, and decreased for six.

cost.quote: each editing run was limited to 32,768 Editor output tokens, 300 Editor CPU calls, and six hours

baselines_and_controls: Original unedited Qwen3.5-0.8B paired on same server, problems and sampling seeds; original evaluated twice per combination (identical in 286 of 300). No random-edit, fine-tune, LoRA or prompting baselines.
runs_and_variance: 10 editing runs (seeds 1-10), each tested on 50 problems x 3 test seeds; ten test seeds for three selected problems; descriptive counts only, per-seed results in Tables 1, 5, 6 (e.g. technically correct per seed 22-32 of 150 edited).
robustness_of_edits: not tested (no fine-tuning or quantization tests); test set held out from Editor but some test problems share procedures with editing problems
verification: none (automated grader plus retrospective manual review of format-rejected answers; Codex-assisted trace review)
memorization_vs_reasoning: n/a for the Editor; for the target, separates 'finish an already computed answer' (36 of 64) from 'corrected computation' (13 of 64).
limitations_stated: One Target and one Editor; same 50 test problems, three sampling seeds; test problems known to the author and some revised during development; some test problems share procedures with editing problems; AST-based repetition can miss equivalent code; only selected traces reviewed for follow-up checkpoints; magnitude varied across editing runs.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 Sparks of Weight-Space Programming blog [3]
Hu et al. Exploring Weight-Space Programming arXiv:2611.09382 [4]
notes_for_survey: Traces executed Python code and outputs before and after Claude-made edits to Qwen3.5-0.8B, separating gains from submitting already-computed values versus changed computations. Three of four initial checkpoints changed only the final-block MLP down-projection, the same matrix reported edited in Hu et al.'s math runs.
